title: Lord Ye Loves Dragons
text:
Lord Ye, a nobleman of the state of She, was famous for his love of dragons. He had dragons carved on his belt hooks and wine vessels and painted on the walls and beams of his house. Everyone knew that no one adored dragons more than he did.

A real dragon in heaven heard about this and was touched. It flew down to visit its admirer. It put its head in through Lord Ye's window and let its tail trail through the hall. When Lord Ye saw it, he turned pale, lost his wits and ran away in terror. What he loved, the story concludes, was not dragons at all but things that looked like dragons.

In the collection where Liu Xiang preserved the tale, it is told by Zizhang, a disciple of Confucius. He had traveled far to visit Duke Ai of Lu, who was known to praise scholars, and had waited seven days without being received. Leaving, he sent the duke this story, saying that the duke loved men who resembled scholars, not real ones.
lesson: Saying you want independent thinkers or bold ideas is easy. Notice how you react when one actually shows up in your office, and whether you welcome it or retreat.
people: Lord Ye (Zigao) of She, Zizhang, Duke Ai of Lu
source: Liu Xiang, Xinxu (New Prefaces), compiled 1st century BC
